outcome: Every blocker occurrence encountered during an atom carries immutable work-memory run plus atom request, run, and attempt identity; Atom Controller preserves a canonical blocker-closeout summary during validation and refuses completion or successor authorization while any linked occurrence lacks an allowed disposition.
practical_value: A passed implementation cannot silently leave its own deliverable blocker unresolved, lose an incidental defect without an owner, or authorize the next atom from a stale self-attestation.
stopping_condition: Open, fixed-awaiting-verification, and verified deliverable blockers prevent completion; closed requires remaining_work none; superseded requires an existing successor occurrence bound to the same atom; open incidental defects require explicit downstream ownership; non-gap requires recorded evidence; validation preserves the canonical closeout result and authorization independently rechecks the live canonical ledger with zero orphaned or undispositioned linked occurrences.

captured_cases.expected_outcome: Every open, fixed-awaiting-verification, or verified deliverable occurrence blocks completion and authorization through the real Atom Controller and blocker-catalog CLIs.
Closed, evidenced non-gap, valid same-atom supersession, and explicitly downstream-owned incidental occurrences produce a preserved clear summary and permit live rechecked authorization.
